evidence: Fresh pinned-image reads show relocated code pointers at base table 0x669408/0x66940C targeting 0x404250/0x404270, followed by nonrelocated vbtable words -4 and 0x18. Derived table 0x66EAE8/0x66EAEC targets 0x5D4890/0x5D4990, followed by nonrelocated -4 and 0x34. This independently bounds both primary tables to two slots. Original remove_all at 0x402992 invokes primary slot 1 with the entry payload, then destroys payload and entry via their virtual allocation bases. The candidate src/alphanet.h currently declares only unk_slot0.

Native inspect of 0x5D4990 confirms receiver field +0x18 gates cleanup; when it is zero, payload pointers +4 and +8 are individually freed at 0x5D49A4/0x5D49BB and nulled. src/recovered/005d4990.cpp retains a BYTE_EXACT seed with precisely this behavior, while src/unrecovered/005d4890.cpp and its original code create/copy those two strings using the list allocator. This is a source-model recovery direction, not evidence that the current ledger lifetime is accepted.
payload.hypothesis: Recover the AlphaNet ledger two-slot virtual surface and allocator-aware payload cleanup as one ownership change. Use the existing exact cleanup seed at 0x5D4990 instead of a new raw-address bridge, and retain its historical obligation while recovering the real receiver and payload fields. Establish the base-versus-derived storage split and allocation-aware node deletion before replacing list cleanup; do not restore a one-slot placeholder or manually install original tables.
